items.title: 8.10 Position of equilibrium and reaction conditions

source_refs.note: Topic 8.10, printed page 179. The print's two bullets state the directions the opposite way round; the lesson gives the conventional sense.

blocks.text: The position of equilibrium is the relative amounts of products and reactants in an equilibrium mixture. When a system at equilibrium is disturbed, the position may move: if the concentration of products rises relative to the reactants the position has shifted to the right (the print says left); if the concentration of products falls relative to the reactants it has shifted to the left (the print says right).

blocks.prompt: A mixture of N2, H2 and NH3 at equilibrium is compressed and the proportion of ammonia rises. In which direction has the position of equilibrium shifted, and has Kc changed?
blocks.explanation: Towards the products, to the right, since the proportion of ammonia has risen. Kc is unchanged: only the temperature can alter it; the pressure change altered the concentrations so that their ratio gives the same Kc.

items: Position of equilibrium: relative amounts of products and reactants; a shift to the right means more products, to the left more reactants (the print's two statements are reversed).
